# Decisions made during the v1 build

The build's running log, kept as written: each entry says what was decided and why. Items marked FOR MARTIN are listed in the v1 PR.

- powerbi: the mock requires PKCE (S256) on authorize for every client, stricter than Microsoft, which lets confidential clients skip it; the product always sends S256, so a product that dropped PKCE fails its tests. Stops being right if the product ever needs a client without PKCE.
- powerbi: Power BI enumerations in the mirror are lower snake_case, mapped by the sync (column_type data/calculated/calculated_table_column/row_number; principal type user/group/app).
- powerbi: `powerbi.sync.workspaces.include` is "all" or a list of workspace ids, default "all"; an empty list syncs nothing.
- access: `sign_in.passkeys` defaults to false.
- access: the CLI is the first-party public OAuth client `pbmb-cli`; endpoints discovered through RFC 8414 metadata; the device grant answers access and refresh tokens with the same rotation as MCP grants.
- security: no directory named `identity` in the repository (the agents' deny rule and .gitignore treat it as an age identity); the mock's Microsoft identity code lives in `src/entra/`.
- security: example env files are `env.example` (no leading dot) so agents, which may not read `.env*`, can write them; compose files are checked with `--dry-run create`, never `config`.
- security: `applyGrants` revokes everything from `public`, including execute on non-extension routines; a routine the roles call needs a declared grant.
- architecture: the image sets NODE_ENV=production; dev and test overlays override.
- architecture: the dev mock sits on `egress` only, never on the internal `app` network.
- look: `@theme inline reference` in the tokens' Tailwind mapping, so no self-referencing variables are emitted.
- standards: TypeScript files kebab-case; ordinary tests `<module>.test.ts`; security tests `<name>_security_test.ts` (module as spelled, or property in snake_case).
- budgets: CLI core 1,302 of 900 (refresh contract added mid-run), api core 2,151 of 1,800, mock core 3,240 of 1,600 (raised to 3,300: fidelity across five Microsoft surfaces).
- security: the worker rotates its own age identity under row-level security: `worker_rw` may update only `secret_ciphertext` rows with `reader = 'worker'` and insert or update only its own `container_identity` rows; a compromised worker cannot overwrite the api's ciphertexts (e.g. forge CSV links by replacing `result_link_key`). Policies live in `apps/api/src/db/sql/secrets.sql`.
- security: `worker_rw` holds nothing on `person_identity` (only the api uses it) [mirror follow-up].
- security: the guarded fetcher's fixed-host profile allows private addresses (Power BI Private Link, private endpoints); its controls are https, the configured-origin allowlist, no redirects, size and time limits. Only `fetchUntrusted` (client-chosen URLs) refuses private addresses. Stops being right if a fixed host's URL ever becomes something a client can choose.
- architecture: the guarded fetcher uses `undici` 8.12.3 (pinned) for DNS-pinned connections.
- docs: the README frames the product as Agent First BI (Martin, 2026-10-25); only the README, no rename.
- access: Cerbos layering by scope: defaults at the root scope; a deployment's own policies in scope `deployment`; every request names `deployment`; lenient scope search falls back to the defaults. A deployment policy overrides or narrows with `scopePermissions`.
- access: a service account may describe and query only the workspaces and apps its admin gave it, in every visibility mode; a deployment policy can narrow it, never widen it.
- powerbi (mock): Build is required to query (workspace Admin/Member/Contributor, a share or app audience whose right includes Explore); measure DAX in INFO views only for Admin/Member/Contributor; row-level security roles are not modelled (the product relies on Power BI applying RLS through each person's token).
- book: `worker_rw` may delete from `event` (90-day retention, run by the worker's expire job); `book_change` stays insert-only.
- access: `@cerbos/core` 0.33.1 added (plan types).
- process: jobs (i-8o4o) took a third review round, against the two-round rule, because the second review's findings were new defects in the newly added locking and every later issue waits on it.
- book: categories and terms are written only by the api; the worker reads them to build search documents for the embedder.
- powerbi: Power BI's 401 means a stale delegated token: the query service refreshes once and retries, a second 401 answers not_found, invalid_grant answers needs_connection; 403 and 404 answer not_found (like a missing dataset); a rejected app or scanner client secret is a configuration conflict for the admin.
- book: the conventions gained five keys beyond the spec's YAML so no rule lives in code: `naming.qualifiers`, `naming.money_qualifier.units`, `not_the_same_as.ignore_words`, `term_fields.definition`, `term_fields.values`. The image ships `conventions/presets/` at `/app/conventions/presets`.
- architecture: the image mirrors the repository's layout under `/app` (`/app/apps/api/dist`, `/app/apps/api/src/db/sql`, `/app/access/policies`, `/app/conventions/presets`), so module-relative paths work from source and from the image.
- book: a company may set its own qualifier groups from any preset; only the groups named in `qualifier_order` must have words. A required field that is empty or whitespace counts as missing everywhere.
- process: the book curation issue (i-2bnn) blew its budget on the mirror read services alone; it was split, with categories, terms, docs and the conventions service moved to i-1mxo (curation_terms). Categories and docs have no event kind in the spec's list, so their changes write book_change only.
- budgets: categories and terms (i-1mxo) came in at about 2,670 net lines against 1,400 even after the split; accepted with a review mandated to cut duplication (paging helpers copied from read.ts). The decomposition underestimated the book's curation services by about half.

## Tests and the sync (wave after the drafter)
- The api's test files share one database and run in parallel. Tests that load the sample tenant run in one transaction that always rolls back, as a test-only `test_runner` role (made by `test/database.ts`, never by the stack's init script) that switches to the role under test. Under `DATABASE_URL` the server's owner must create `test_runner` and set `TEST_RUNNER_PASSWORD`.
- Tests that put the sample's fixed ids in the database take turns on one advisory lock (`takeSampleTurn`), so two of them cannot deadlock.
- The sync stores workspaces one transaction after another, never two at once; scans still overlap (four in flight). Simpler and lets the sync run inside a test's rolled-back transaction.
- Curation of metrics waits for curation of categories and terms (a dependency the decomposition lacked): the shared helpers (`requireCurator`, `visibleMetric`, the paging helpers) land there.
- The DAX module was merged unformatted; formatted on build/v1 (539fd29).
- Curation of metrics hit its 1,500-line budget with only `metrics.ts` (975 lines) and the approval security test written. Split: i-4ku3 keeps metrics (budget raised to 1,900); variants and the next drafts are a new issue, i-4ssd (curation_variants, 1,100), which the MCP tools issue now also depends on.
- A merge is refused when one metric has a unit and the other has none, not only when two units differ: the spec says a wrong merge is worse than a missed one, so the curator sets the draft's unit first. For Martin to confirm.
- `list_metrics`: `include_children` defaults to false; the trust filter is the list `trust_states`, as `list_terms` and `search` take it (the spec's filter list says `trust_state`).
- Sync came to 1,506 lines (budget 1,300) and sign-in to about 1,640 (budget 1,500); both accepted as overruns.
- The sync's removal is soft: a workspace, dataset, table, column or measure the sync no longer sees gets `removed_at`; only access-list rows and app-dataset rows are deleted. No sync path moves or deletes a variant. A full sync also marks removed the workspaces that the include or exclude settings now leave out (spec steps 2 and 4).
- A job's handler receives the job's own `trigger` beside its args, so the sync's trigger is stated once (in the queue), not repeated in args.
- Power BI enumerations are mapped to lower snake_case once, in the scanner's schema; the test fixture imports that mapping.
- `access.default_role` applies only when no other assignment reaches a person, as the spec's Roles section says (the issue said "plus").
- Agents never write to sudocode (the build README); the coordinator sets every status. Earlier dispatch prompts said otherwise; corrected from the sync wave on.
- Only a person can set `human_verified`, whatever the conventions say: `trust.human_verify_from: any` widens it from the browser to a person's token (MCP, CLI, API), never to a service account. Code, with a security test.
- Curation answers never name what the caller may not describe: a check's message names only labels of metrics the caller can see, and a refused merge names only describable measures and datasets and counts the rest.
- Sign-in security review (two high, six medium findings), decided by the coordinator for Martin's review:
  - `role_assignment` gains a `provider` column, required for group assignments: a group matches only within the provider that issued it (`microsoft` for Entra). The spec's `role_assignment` shape changes.
  - Person and email-domain assignments match only a verified email; a Microsoft email counts as verified only from the configured tenant.
  - Sessions last 12 hours from sign-in with no sliding renewal; a passkey sign-in needs a provider sign-in within 7 days; groups read at a sign-in are ignored after 7 days.
  - Only an allow-list of Better Auth endpoints is served; ID-token sign-in is off; implicit account linking is off; passkeys require user verification.
  - Sign-in rate limits are stored in Postgres; `TRUSTED_PROXY` (bootstrap, optional) says which proxy's `X-Forwarded-For` to trust.
  - Open for Martin: B2B guests carry the tenant's `tid`, so they count as tenant members (`everyone_in_tenant`, `access.default_role`). Left as is.
- The conventions test "keeps every version, records each change and announces it" failed once in the sync agent's 27 runs; 20 runs on build/v1 since were all green. Unreproduced; watch it.
- Sign-in took three review rounds (an exception to the two-round rule, as jobs did): the issue review, a security review with 2 high and 6 medium findings, and a security re-review that found the shipped compose made every sign-in share one rate limit. `TRUSTED_PROXY` is now passed by compose, the `edge` subnet is pinned, and the deploy guides set it per target.
- A Google sign-in matches an email-domain assignment only when the token's `hd` is that domain.
- Curation of variants came to 1,279 lines (budget 1,100), accepted. Its review found a deadlock between two opposite variant moves and one between the drafter and a curator's move; both now lock metrics in id order before variants, with race tests.
- Two drafter guards have no test: it files a group only under a metric it locked, and it skips an empty draft another transaction holds (deleting it on a later run). A test would have to commit an empty draft that every other test file's drafter run sees.
- Tests that read events take the event lock first (`test/events.ts`, `eventsSince`), so events other files commit cannot reach them; with a file committing events throughout, the suite stayed green.
- The api suite's test timeout is 30 s, not vitest's 5 s: tests that load the sample tenant take turns, and a book change waits for the event lock another file's rolled-back transaction holds. Postgres still reports a real deadlock within a second. Before it, about 1 run in 8 timed out.
- `freshPeer` draws each test client address at random from 198.18.0.0/15: rate limits count per address in the shared database and outlive a run by a minute.
- MCP OAuth (i-6b4u) hit its 1,500-line budget with the device test, authorization tests and threat model left; raised to 2,200 because none of that may be cut. Scopes are `mcp`, `api` and `offline_access`. Dynamic client registration is exempt from the origin check (native MCP clients send no Origin; a registration grants nothing until a person allows it). Better Auth leaves JWT access tokens working after refresh-token reuse (#11317), so the token endpoint is wrapped: a token works only while the person's consent to that client stands, and reuse revokes the consent.
- The origin check (CSRF) guards requests a browser's cookie authenticates. A request with an `Authorization: Bearer` header (MCP clients, the CLI, service accounts) needs no Origin: a cross-site page cannot add that header without a CORS preflight the api never allows. The spec said "every state-changing request except the token and device endpoints", which would have refused every MCP and CLI write.
- Power BI connection: `invalid_client` and `unauthorized_client` from Microsoft answer 409 (the admin's to fix: the app registration), not `needs_reconnect` for the person. A spec change.
- A connection's Microsoft identity counts the person as a tenant member only while their groups were read within 7 days, as a sign-in's groups do; a disconnect or `invalid_grant` ends it.
- `rekey_tokens` seals only with the key the api holds in memory, runs only once the api has restarted with the new key (enqueued at api start), and keeps a retired key file while any row is still sealed for it.
- TODO coordinator: `app.ts` `onError` logs `error.stack`; a `DrizzleQueryError` message carries the query's parameters (tokens' ciphertext, PKCE verifiers). Log the cause, not the parameters, after MCP OAuth and the connection merge.
- MCP OAuth security review (1 high, 4 medium): the token endpoint refuses repeated form fields and anything but form-urlencoded; a lost concurrent refresh revokes the grant; registration refuses back-channel logout and `jwks_uri`; metadata-document fetch errors never name an address; the device flow takes no caller-chosen `user_id`, returns no `verification_uri_complete`, is claimed only by a person typing the code, and shows when and from where it started. Budget raised to 2,700.
- Open for Martin, raised again by the connection's security review (Medium, older code): Entra B2B guests carry the host tenant's `tid`, so they count as tenant members (`everyone_in_tenant`, `access.default_role`) at sign-in and at connect. Checking the `acct` claim (0 member, 1 guest) would separate them; it needs the optional claim enabled on the app registration.
- Open, documented: the keep-alive renews the refresh token of a person no role reaches on every run (the Graph read), with no end date.
- TODO coordinator (with the onError fix): `secret_ciphertext` writes in `secrets/store.ts:176` and `secrets/rotate.ts:77` put ciphertext bytes into a failing query's error message.
- Connection came to about 2,400 lines (budget 1,400), for the same reason.
- Each api test file gets its own database, cloned from a template migrated once per run (the build README's first design, as Metrics Book does). Before it, files shared one database and met on locks, fixed sample ids, committed jobs and counters; about one run in five failed on a slow machine. The earlier workarounds (`takeSampleTurn`, `eventsSince`, `privateQueue`) are removed in a cleanup once no agent edits tests.
- A service account never holds `admin` (a database CHECK) and is refused every admin action and `book:edit_conventions` in code, whatever a deployment's policies say: a leaked admin key could otherwise mint itself new keys forever. The spec allowed `pbmb sa create --role <role>` with any role. A read-only status check by a service account needs its own action (the admin issue).
- `source_cidrs` is refused while `TRUSTED_PROXY` is unset: behind a proxy the api sees only the proxy's address. Lowering an account's `max_key_age_days` takes effect on existing keys at once.
- Done: the `onError` TODO. One error logger (`http/error-log.ts`) for routes, MCP tools and Better Auth (`onAPIError.throw`) logs a failed query as Postgres's own error, never its query or parameters (which can carry ciphertext, PKCE verifiers, key digests, secret ciphertext).
- The connector's surface test follows every import with the TypeScript checker to its declaration; a tool reaches only the reads on its list. `typescript` 6.0.3 is a dev dependency of `apps/api` for it.
- Role names: a shipped role (`viewer`, `curator`, `admin`) is assigned as is; any other well-formed name needs an explicit custom flag (`pbmb admin roles assign ... --custom`), so typos are refused while a company's own roles still need no code. `access.default_role` is `none`, `viewer` or `curator`, never `admin`.
- A service account may hold a role the policies grant `admin:read_status` (the spec's read-only deployment check); every other admin action stays refused to service accounts in code.
- Admin services: budget raised from 1,300 to 1,550 for export and import.
- Visibility fails closed: a Power BI access entry counts only with a right that is neither missing nor `None` (Microsoft's key for the right varies), and a person's own Microsoft object id counts only while it is fresh (a Microsoft sign-in or groups read within 7 days), as tenant membership does.
- `importBook` is additive: it adds and changes what the file holds and never removes what it leaves out.
- `admin` is assigned only to a person or a group, never to `everyone_in_tenant` or an email domain (a database CHECK). The last-admin rule counts person assignments only, and the setup link reopens by the same rule.
- A check result is a fixed sentence of at most 300 characters (a database CHECK) and never holds any piece of the value it checked.
- `admin:read_status` alone (a read-only role or service account) sees the sync's status without its error, failing check names without messages, expiring secrets by name and date, and a count of connections to remake; a caller who can manage settings sees everything. The `/me` expiry warning goes to those who can manage secrets.
- An import needs the admin action for each kind it changes (settings, people, service accounts, conventions), runs setting checks in its preview, and writes its audit lines after commit with one `import_id`; a failed import leaves one "rolled back" line. `setup.*` keys never travel in `book.yml`.
- For Martin: the spec's Cerbos table lacks the new actions `admin:read_status`, `admin:run_check`, `admin:export_book`, `admin:import_book`.
- FOR MARTIN, a tension between two approved defaults: the query log is readable by everyone signed in (decision 6), while people see only the metadata Power BI lets them reach. Under `metadata_visibility: powerbi`, query log search shows the dataset names and DAX of datasets the reader cannot reach. Built as approved; changing it is one Cerbos rule or a filter to describable datasets, which the coordinator would recommend.
- Queries came to 2,270 lines (budget 1,600). A spent daily row budget answers `rate_limited` (with when it frees up). `query_log` gains `dataset_name` and `result_expires_at`.
- Threads came to about 1,400 (budget 1,000).
- Queries security review (7 medium): a service account is refused on a row-level-security model by the api itself, before any token; previews and pages stay within 16 KiB even for one huge row; the row budget reserves the maximum per query in flight (at most 4 in flight per principal); `purpose` is capped at 2,000 characters and NUL refused; CSV cells starting `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR get a leading `'` (formula injection; recorded in `docs/decisions/queries.md`); Power BI's error sentence in the log is shown only to the query's own principal (it can quote a cell value).
- Queries' final size: 2,888 lines (budget raised to 2,800 for the security fixes, 88 over; accepted). The 4-in-flight cap answers `rate_limited` like a spent budget. A refused query's log entry keeps up to 100 KB of its input, so the log shows what was refused.
- The per-file test databases made the old test locks and private queues unneeded; they are removed (`takeSampleTurn`, the event lock, `privateQueue`), and `freshPeer` counts. The suite ran 902, then 935, all green.
- Setup security review (4 medium): the setup API moves to `/api/setup/*` (`/setup` is the screen), and the link puts its token in the fragment (`/setup#token=`), so no proxy log records it. Before the first admin exists, the setup session may run only the address and app-registration steps; every other step needs an admin's browser session. The setup session lives at most 12 hours from the link's spend; a new link revokes every earlier link and session. The first-admin marker is bound to the holder's own OAuth `state`, and the step asks the holder to confirm the admitted email before it makes the admin (a login CSRF with a planted cookie from a sibling subdomain could otherwise make the attacker admin). The app-registration check is an allowlist of the spec's delegated scopes, and refuses any application permission (`roles`) on either registration. The worker writes only its own `setting_check` rows (row-level security). The Power BI token cache is keyed by authority, tenant, client id and the secret's digest.
- Relationships on demand: only Power BI refusing the INFO functions (a 400) marks a dataset `unavailable` for everyone. A 403 or 404 is about the asking person's own rights (no Build right, a missing scope), so it answers unknown for that person and leaves the dataset to be read by someone who can. A spec amendment to "Relationships and display folders" item 3. A failing read is tried at most once per person and dataset per 5 minutes.
- FOLLOW-UP (not built): a dataset whose scan result carries relationships is never read with INFO views, so its measures' display folders stay null. Reading `INFO.VIEW.MEASURES()` alone for those needs a column of its own (`folders_read_at`). The scanner's schema does not document `relationships`, so this is rare.
- Setup's final size: about 2,800 lines (budget 1,500), two security reviews, approved. At start the api revokes every earlier unspent link, but an open setup session survives a restart, within its 12 hours.
- Accepted, documented in B9: during the 10 minutes of the first admin's sign-in, someone who can send the holder's browser to Microsoft's callback can expire the marker cookie, so the holder signs in again (a denial of service only; nobody else can become admin).
- FOR MARTIN, before release: the app-registration check reads Power BI scopes as full URIs (`https://analysis.windows.net/powerbi/api/Dataset.Read.All`). If a real tenant's token answer lists them in short form, the check refuses a correct registration (it fails closed). Check once against a real tenant; the mock decides the tests.
- Backups dump as the `migrator` role: `setting_check` has row-level security, so another role's `pg_dump` fails on it (in the deploy guides).
- Done: see the first_sync line below.
- The dev stack publishes only the api's port and the mock's (api + 1); Postgres stays on the internal network. `sample_data` is true when `powerbi.authority`'s host is localhost, `*.localhost` or a loopback address, which only the mock can be (outside development, the authority must be https to Microsoft's hosts). The api sets `Secure` cookies always; Chrome and Firefox accept them on http://localhost, and Safari may not.
- Embedder: about 1,980 lines plus the trigger round (budget 1,100; tests about 870), accepted. A spec change: the spec re-embeds "on the next sync", so a curated description would stay unsearchable until then. Instead every `book_change` queues one `embed` request in the same transaction (at most one queued at a time), and the job reads `book_change` past a cursor it keeps, rebuilding only those elements' documents. The sync's run still rebuilds everything and compares hashes, since mirror changes write no `book_change`. The event feed stays as the spec lists it; `book_change` is the book's change log.
- Dev stack: 756 lines (budget 600, then 700), accepted with its two extra tests. `dev:up` finishes 9 of 10 setup steps on the mock; `agents` waits for a connector sign-in. The compose security test now reads `!reset` as Compose does (the value is dropped), so a reset hardening key in `compose.yml` fails it. Root `engines` is Node 24.2 or later (`import.meta.main`).
- Done: a sync with no scanner set up is recorded as skipped with its reason, and the setup's first_sync step starts a sync only for `start_sync: true` (polls start nothing; a failure stays visible). Its check reports a queued sync before an earlier failure.
- Security, found by the embedder's review: an admin could set `search.base_url` (and, in older code, `powerbi.authority`, `powerbi.api_url`, `powerbi.graph_url`) to a host of their own, and the api would send the embedding key or a registration's secret there. That broke "admins can replace a secret but never read one back". These four settings are now set only in the environment, by the operator; the store refuses them and ignores a saved row (a security test). A sovereign cloud or a proxy is configured in the deployment's `.env`.
- Search documents: a metric's text no longer lists its variants' measure names (a spec change), since a person who sees the metric through one dataset could otherwise find measure names from a dataset they cannot see. `search_text` is capped at 8,000 UTF-8 bytes; a text the provider refuses keeps no vector, and the run goes on. A variant in a personal workspace leaves the workspace's name (its owner's) out of the provider's text.
- Security, older code, found by the embedder's re-review: an admin could point a sign-in provider at an issuer of their own (or change its kind under the same id) and receive its client secret at the token exchange. Moving a provider to another issuer or kind, or removing it, now deletes its secret in the same transaction, in the admin section and in a book.yml import; the admin enters the secret again for the new issuer.
- Embedding refusals: a text is held to be at fault only after a fixed probe sentence succeeds in the same run; otherwise the run fails and nothing is marked. Refused batches split in halves, and a run has a 10-minute budget, after which it queues its successor.
- Embedder's final size: about 3,400 lines with tests and docs (budget 1,100), after two security reviews and two code reviews, all approved. Known gap: when a full embed run runs out of its 10-minute budget while a changes-only request is already queued, the rest waits for the next sync's run (at most an hour on the default schedule).
- Scheduling: the REST write routes and the connector's tools started beside search rather than after it. Neither needs search except the `search` tool itself, which the tools' agent adds once search merges.
- 2026-10-26: the first session stopped at 03:19 on the account's weekly usage limit with search, the REST write routes and the connector's tools mid-task. Their unfinished work was saved as one WIP commit on each old agent branch, and fresh implementers resumed on top of it. The connector tools' budget rose from 1,300 to 1,800 lines (26 tools; the WIP alone was about 1,440).
- Connector tools, first reviews (code and security): CHANGES. The widened surface allowlist gave the connector the whole result store and a raw CSV-link signer (High). It is replaced by context-bound `readResult` and `resultCsvLink`, and `writeAudit` by one fixed `recordConnectorReached`, deduplicated per principal and client per 24 h so whoami cannot grow the audit log without bound. Budget raised to 2,400 for the fix round (refusal tests for every tool, input caps). Accepted: the setup `agents` check takes the admin role as held when the check runs, not when whoami was called.
- FOR MARTIN: the connector surface test's ALLOWED list grows by the book, mirror, query-log and thread reads plus the two result functions and the audit function. agents.md rule 2 says you approve each addition; they are listed in the PR.
- REST write routes: the issue said approve takes a session cookie only, but the spec's `trust.human_verify_from: any` allows approval from the CLI and API. The route no longer checks `via` itself; the approve service decides from the conventions. `GET /metrics/{name}/checks` had no service, so `metricChecks` was added to the metrics service. Shared route helpers live in `routes/v1/adapter.ts`. Budget raised from 1,200 to 1,650 lines.
- REST routes declare their success and error answers as zod schemas, type-checked against the handler's answer, because the SPA's types are generated from the OpenAPI file and the write routes set the pattern for the read and admin routes. Budget raised to 2,700 for this and the security round.
- CSV download audit: a link download is recorded with `detail.by = "csv_link"` and the client address, never as the owner's own request. Refusals are audited wherever a principal is known; a bad signature with no credential is not (the audit row needs a principal) and is bounded by the per-address limit. On the link path the owner is re-checked (a person with no role, a disabled or deleted service account, or one outside its source_cidrs gets nothing).
- FOLLOW-UP (not built): the book's free-text columns (definitions, descriptions, notes) have no length CHECK in the database; the route and tool inputs cap them at 20,000 characters.
- Connector tools merged without `search` (840a42e); the api suite ran 1,095 tests, all green. The issue stays open until the `search` tool lands.
- Search, first reviews: CHANGES. The vector side now uses the HNSW index with pgvector's iterative scan (the first build was a filtered brute-force scan, about 300 MB read per search at 50,000 documents). Older code, found by search's review: `inApp` resolved any app with no visibility or removal check, so an app filter told a person whether a hidden app existed (also in dataset, metric and term lists); it now answers a hidden app like a missing one. A failed query embedding (any cause, including a fetcher timeout) falls back to words. Search gets input bounds, a per-principal rate limit and a statement timeout. Budget raised from 700 to 1,300.
- REST answers are parsed through their zod schema before they leave, so an undeclared field never reaches a client; shared entities and the error body are named components in the OpenAPI document. Link and credential CSV downloads share one per-owner budget, and IPv6 addresses are limited per /64. Older code: deleting a service account now deletes its results, so a new account reusing the name inherits nothing. REST write routes' budget raised to 3,000.
- REST write routes merged (d19ba9a); the api suite ran 1,125 tests, all green. The single migration was regenerated for a `query_log.via` CHECK.
- Scheduling: the REST read routes and the admin routes started side by side once the write routes set the pattern; they share no files. The read routes leave `GET /search` until search merges, and whichever of the two merges second regenerates `openapi.json`. The shared response schemas move into `routes/v1/schemas.ts`.
- Security, older code, found by search's re-review: the guarded fetcher built its Request outside its try, so a stored API key holding a newline would reach the error log whole through Node's header error. The fetcher now answers a fixed sentence for any unexpected error, and secret writes refuse control characters.
- FOR MARTIN (agents.md rule 2): two security tests changed in the search branch. `search_visibility_security_test.ts` now expects the outsider to find a term backed by a Sales column, since terms are visible to everyone signed in (the book's rule; a term's search text holds only its own words). `embedder_security_test.ts` runs its Retry-After test on document embeds, plus a new check that a query embed never waits.
- REST read routes: `custom` filters are query parameters `custom.<key>=<value>` (the spec's own form), `trust_states` comma-separated. The change feed shows a thread event to whoever may see its element, and `sync.*` events need the new Cerbos action `admin:read_sync_events` (admins hold it through `admin.yaml`'s `*`). FOR MARTIN: add `admin:read_sync_events` to the spec's Cerbos table. Budget raised from 900 to 1,250.
- Test environment: from about 12:00 on 2026-10-26 the api tests timed out and lost their Postgres mid-run. Docker's VM (7.75 GiB) also held about 49 containers of another project's test runs (`mb_*`), and the test Cerbos was killed at its 128 MB limit. The test Cerbos now gets the stack's 256 MB (21ff38e), idle per-checkout test stacks are taken down once their branch merges, and reviewers run only their branch's test files. FOR MARTIN: the other project's leftover test containers (`mb_api_test_*`, `mb-anfra-check-*`) hold most of Docker's memory; they were left alone.

The setup step's first sync and the admin sync share one `startSync`, enqueued in one statement so parallel requests queue one sync. Budget raised to 2,000.
- Change feed, security review: an event's payload carries ids, never another element's name (a merge into a visible metric used to name the merged-away draft, often a measure name from a hidden dataset). Metric events record their dataset scope when written, so an event about a since-deleted metric still reaches exactly those who could see it. `sync.*` errors go only to callers who may manage settings. Older code: an app's docs and a dataset's app list now show only apps the caller may see (`appsSeen`). Read routes' budget raised to 1,800.
- Search (19c47ba), the admin routes with the checked-in OpenAPI file (2a5c152) and the connector's `search` tool (52598a7) merged; all 27 connector tools are in, and the surface test requires exactly the spec's list. - CLI security review: ids and names went into URL paths unescaped, and httpx collapses `..` and cuts at `#`, so `pbmb admin secrets set '../settings/x#'` would have sent a typed secret to the settings route. One path builder in the CLI core quotes every segment, and every command uses it. `pbmb init` pins the core image by digest from a bundled `image.lock` that the release workflow writes (i-5ajf must write it); without one, `init` needs `--image` with a digest. Human-readable output strips terminal control characters; the CSV download refuses a link on another origin and writes through a private temp file. The CLI's shared helpers live in core modules (`answers.py`, `tables.py`, `csv_download.py`, `deployment.py`). The queries/admin CLI issue's budget rose from 1,600 to 3,000 for its ten command groups.

Files a command sends (`docs set --file`, `dax run --file`) must be regular UTF-8 files under 1 MiB and never the CLI's own credentials file. `columns` and `measures` take a dataset by id or name through one shared lookup.

- FOR MARTIN (security design): the api holds MIGRATOR_DATABASE_URL because the spec has it migrate at start (spec lines 209, 259). - Stack lock incident: preview_stop killed only the lock wrapper, so `dev:serve` never took its stack down. The orphaned stack (pbmb_f7b30a77) then kept every waiter out for about 50 minutes. The wrapper now runs the command in the background, forwards TERM and INT to it, and waits for its cleanup before releasing the lock.

  - the scanner check queues atomically (it uses the tenant's admin API quota), records who asked and is audited on the setup path;
  - a check queued for over 90 s with no worker answers a failing "worker did not run" result;

  - High: Azure's one managed identity read every secret, so the api could read the worker's identity. Now three identities with per-secret roles. VM backups were unencrypted and deletable from the VM. Now age-encrypted to off-VM recipients, with write-only credentials and bucket-side retention.
  - Medium: VM restore can no longer overwrite production; Railway keys stay out of the repository; Railway's sealed-variable identity is the default (no root); Azure egress, Cerbos as root and the identity storage account are locked down or stated; Dokploy's shared control-plane network is stated; the setup link comes from `server setup-link`, never logs; Caddy runs non-root with TRUSTED_PROXY as its single address.
  - Product follow-ups queued after i-1t4i merges: stop logging the setup link at startup (log only that one exists); refuse `SampleOnly` values in production config.
- CLIENT_ADDRESS_HEADER=x-real-ip (for Railway): Railway's docs say the edge sets X-Real-IP, but not that it overwrites a value the client sends, and nobody here can test a live Railway account. The mode stays opt-in. /api/v1/me now returns the `client_address` the api settled on, so an operator can check with a forged X-Real-IP before relying on the mode, and the Railway guide makes that check a step. Service-account `source_cidrs` stays refused under this mode. TRUSTED_PROXY together with x-real-ip is refused at startup. The threat model lists what a route past the edge allows. FOR MARTIN: run the /me check on the first real Railway deployment.
- Web e2e is split in two. The first-run setup spec needs a stack with no admin, and every other spec needs the seeded `dev:up` stack. A bare `playwright test` runs everything except first-run. `pnpm --filter web test:e2e` runs both phases in order (no-setup stack and first-run, then reset, `dev:up`, the rest, check:ui), and check:all will call it. Sign-ins: a sessions project signs in admin, curator and viewer once, and only real sign-in tests are tagged @once. The CLI grant revoke test hit the 5-per-address device lookup limit. With fewer sign-ins no Retry-After wait is needed. Suite time: first-run 49 s, the rest 33 s, check:ui about 92 s.
- i-1t4i security re-review APPROVE. Follow-up (Low, fails closed): a step check's 'own result' compares the worker container's checked_at with the api's requested_at. If the worker's clock runs behind by more than the queue wait, a step can look stuck failing. Use the database's now() for both stamps.

- Research for PII marking and dataset on/off is in. An earlier prototype flags columns only (`is_pii` null, false or true), sets them from the CLI with a name heuristic that only suggests, and lets only `pii.read` holders see flagged columns. Everyone else gets them hidden from metadata and gets a 403 for a query that names one; the check is a regex on bracket tokens. Known gaps to close in our design: measures that use a PII column, and the search and read routes that skip the filter. Datasets have a `visible` switch that hides them everywhere and refuses queries, but keeps syncing; workspaces have their own switch, and turning one off deletes its data on the next sync.
